html:
The Battle of Karbala was fought on 10 October 680, in southern Iraq, between the army of the Umayyad caliph Yazid I and a small band led by Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson of the prophet Muhammad. Husayn's killing there became the event that set Shia Islam apart.

The caliph Muawiya had named his son Yazid as his heir, turning the caliphate into a family inheritance. Many Muslims objected. Husayn, son of Ali and of Muhammad's daughter Fatima, refused to swear loyalty to Yazid. People in Kufa, a city in Iraq loyal to Ali's memory, wrote inviting him to lead them.

Husayn set out from Mecca with his family and a small group of followers. Before he reached Kufa, the Umayyad governor had crushed his supporters there. An Umayyad army stopped Husayn's party on the plain of Karbala, near the Euphrates, and cut them off from the river's water. After days of thirst and failed talks, the army attacked. Husayn and nearly all the men with him were killed. The women and children were taken as captives to Kufa and then to Damascus.

What followed:

  • For the Shia, Husayn is the great martyr, who chose death over submitting to injustice.
  • Every year, on the tenth of the month of Muharram, Shia Muslims mourn him at Ashura, with processions, sermons and passion plays.
  • His tomb at Karbala, the Imam Husayn Shrine, is one of the largest pilgrimage sites in the world.

Karbala turned a political dispute over who should lead into a lasting religious identity, Shia Islam.
